input: with the standby pump on line and the duty pump stopped, the isolation for the seal replacement is applied at the duty pump as follows. The suction valve and the discharge valve at the duty pump are closed, and both valves are locked and tagged in the closed position under the PTW. The motor of the duty pump is also electrically isolated and locked off, so that the pump cannot be started while the isolation is in place. The casing drain is then opened to the closed drain header and is left open. It should be noted that stored pressure can remain trapped in the casing even after the valves have been closed, and for this reason the drain must be proved clear and the pressure proved off before any casing bolt is slackened. The casing is vented through the vent connection until the vent runs dry, after which the vent is closed again and a check is made that no pressure builds up again while the drain is still open. The replacement itself takes about 39 min with the unit isolated, and the isolation is maintained for the whole of that period: neither valve is reopened in the meantime, and the standby pump carries the duty on its own. The isolation is recorded on the PTW, together with the valve positions as they have been left, and the pump is handed over drained, vented and proved, with the first casing bolt
target: with the standby pump on line and the duty pump stopped, the isolation for the seal replacement is applied at the duty pump. Close the suction valve and the discharge valve at the duty pump, and lock and tag both valves in the closed position under the PTW. Isolate the duty pump motor electrically and lock it off, so the pump cannot be started under the isolation. Open the casing drain to the closed drain header and leave the drain open. Stored pressure can remain in the casing after the valves are closed, and the drain is proved clear and the pressure proved off before any casing bolt is slackened. Vent the casing through the vent connection until the vent runs dry, then close the vent and check that no pressure rebuilds with the drain still open. The replacement takes about 39 min with the unit isolated, and the isolation is held for the whole of that time: neither valve is reopened, and the standby pump carries the duty alone. Prove the lines isolated at the pump are the lines tagged, by checking each tag against the isolation list on the PTW. Where the casing drain runs slowly, leave the drain open and wait: a casing that is still draining is not proved. Record the isolation on the PTW, with the valve positions as left, and hand the pump over drained, vented and proved, with the first casing bolt
